finding.title: Localize the hardcoded 'Curriculum settings' tooltip in curriculum_progress_screen.dart
finding.why: Every other string on this screen goes through AppLocalizations (l10n.curriculumProgressBreakdownByLevel, l10n.errorUnknownCurriculum, etc.); this one literal renders in English regardless of device locale, so a Hebrew-locale, RTL user long-pressing the settings gear sees an English tooltip in an otherwise fully-Hebrew screen.
finding.recommendation: Add an ARB key (EN+HE) and use l10n.<key> instead of the literal.
acceptance_criteria: make arb-parity stays green with the new key present in both app_en.arb and app_he.arb.
The tooltip: parameter on this IconButton references an l10n getter, not a string literal.

finding.why: lib/features/parent_mode/ does not exist and never has — the PIN service, PIN flow controller/screen, and parent dashboard aggregator were built directly under features/profiles and features/dashboard. All 9 non-duplicate test files here import from those real locations but live under a phantom 'parent_mode' test-feature directory. Remove the now-empty parent_mode directory and its .gitkeep.
acceptance_criteria: Every relocated test file's import path matches its new test-tree path 1:1 with the lib/ file it targets (AG-5).
git history/blame preserved via git mv for each relocated file.

finding.why: Line 76's test is titled 'deactivates an existing active non-personal track' but its body only inserts a track and asserts getActiveTracks is non-empty — trackDao.deactivateTrack is never invoked. Line 93's test wraps a literally empty async closure (`() async {}()`) in `expectLater(..., completes)`, which is trivially true regardless of any DAO behavior — it doesn't call the DAO at all. finding.title: Delete or wire up the dead TutorAuditLogWriter path (tutor_audit_log_writer.dart / audit_log_providers.dart)
finding.why: A repo-wide grep confirms `TutorAuditLogWriter` is constructed nowhere in lib/ — its 228 lines and the `TutorAuditLogRepository` interface it depends on are unreachable. Its own provider (`tutorAuditLogWriteRepositoryProvider`) resolves to `_StubAuditLogWriteRepository`, a permanent no-op with an ID-less TODO. The class's doc-comment claims 'every tutor write path... calls through this writer' and that entryId format is 'timestamp + 10 random hex chars (26 chars total)', but the actual `_log()` implementation has no random suffix at all — two same-millisecond calls for the same action type would collide on entryId, and per the interface's own idempotency contract ('duplicate writes with the same ULID are silently ignored') the second entry would be silently dropped if this code were ever revived as-is. Cross-checked functions/src/index.ts: the real audit trail is written server-side by each tutor*CF via `writeAuditLog(...)`, so there is no current production gap — this is confusing, misdocumented dead weight, not a live data-loss bug.
finding.recommendation: Delete TutorAuditLogWriter, TutorAuditLogRepository, and the stub/provider if the server-side CF audit writes are now the sole source of truth; if a client-side path is still intended, wire a real Firestore-backed implementation and fix the entryId generator to match its documented ULID claim, with a DNI-#### ticket on the TODO either way.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'TutorAuditLogWriter' lib/ returns nothing, or returns a live call site plus a non-stub repository.
No bare `TODO(...)` without a DNI-#### id remains in audit_log_providers.dart (AG-6 grep clean).

finding.why: make audit check 9/15 only matches a literal single-line `catch (_) {}`; each of these 5 blocks contains ONLY a comment across 2-3 lines and no AppLogger call, no rethrow, and no state-producing action, so they are functionally empty and log-less but invisible to the enforced grep. account_management_service.dart's is on the GDPR-style account-deletion path where a comment literally claims 'Log but don't rethrow' yet no logging call exists. The codebase's own convention for the identical 'best-effort cleanup, may throw PlatformException' shape IS to log (see the ~6 AppLogger.warning(event: '..._sign_out_failed', ...) sites already in sign_in_controller.dart), making these omissions an inconsistency, not a deliberate style choice — any of these silent failures is currently undebuggable from production logs.
finding.recommendation: Add `AppLogger.instance.warning(event: '<descriptive_event>', exception: e)` (or `.handle`) to each; consider extending the Makefile's empty-catch grep to strip `//`-comment lines before matching `{\s*}` so this class of gap is caught going forward.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 5 catch blocks logs via AppLogger
The empty-catch Rule-0 checker is extended to strip comment-only bodies before matching, or a new checker targets this pattern specifically
